<!-- Generated by scripts/env-reference.mjs from docs/env-vars.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Settings go in the `.env` file next to your compose file. The **Compose** column says whether the official compose files pass the variable from `.env` to the container; for the others, add them under `environment:` of the service in a `docker-compose.override.yml`. A variable left empty counts as unset.

This page is generated from `docs/env-vars.json` and checked in CI against the code: adding a variable without documenting it fails the build.

## Deployment

| Variable | Service | Role | Default | Required | Example | Since | Compose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `APP_NAME` | docker compose | Name of the stack in Traefik (router names). Any short word. | – | Traefik only | `looty` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `APP_DOMAIN` | docker compose | Domain name of the instance. Its DNS must point to the machine. | – | yes | `looty.example.org` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `TRAEFIK_NETWORK` | docker compose | Traefik only, with the generator or install.sh --traefik-network: name of the existing external Docker network Traefik uses to reach the stack. The services are attached to it. | – | no | `traefik-public` | 0.50.0 | yes |
| `TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT` | docker compose | Traefik only, with the generator or install.sh --traefik-entrypoint: entry point of your Traefik that serves the routers (usually the HTTPS one). | – | no | `websecure` | 0.50.0 | yes |
| `TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER` | docker compose | Traefik only, with the generator or install.sh --traefik-resolver: certificate resolver of your Traefik for the routers. | – | no | `letsencrypt` | 0.50.0 | yes |
| `LOOTY_VERSION` | docker compose | Version of the Docker images. Set a version number to stay on it. | `latest` | no | `0.33.0` | 0.10.0 | yes |
| `BASE_URL` | backend | Public address of the instance (https://domain, no trailing slash). Used in sign-in redirects, emails and links. | `http://localhost:3000` | yes | `https://looty.example.org` | 0.1.0 | yes |

## Database

| Variable | Service | Role | Default | Required | Example | Since | Compose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LOOTY_DB_DATA` | docker compose | Folder of the host where PostgreSQL stores its data. An absolute path puts it elsewhere. | `./data/postgres` | no | `/srv/looty/postgres` | 0.30.0 | yes |
| `DB_NAME` | docker compose | Name of the PostgreSQL database. | `looty_db` | no | `looty_db` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `DB_USER` | docker compose | PostgreSQL user. | `postgres` | no | `looty_user` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `DB_PASSWORD` | docker compose | PostgreSQL password. Change it. | `postgres` | yes | `a long random password` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `DATABASE_URL` | backend, collaboration | PostgreSQL connection string. The compose files build it from DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD and DB_NAME. The collaboration service falls back to a local development database. | – | yes | `postgres://user:pass@postgres:5432/looty_db` | 0.1.0 | no |

## Sign-in (OpenID Connect)

| Variable | Service | Role | Default | Required | Example | Since | Compose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OIDC_ISSUER` | backend | Address of your OpenID Connect provider (issuer). Read only on the very first start; afterwards edit the provider in Administration. | – | yes | `https://zitadel.example.com` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `OIDC_CLIENT_ID` | backend | Client ID of Looty at the provider. | – | yes | `looty` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` | backend | Client secret of Looty at the provider. | – | yes | – | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `OIDC_PROVIDER_ID` | backend | Fixed UUID of the provider, to know the redirect URL (BASE_URL/api/auth/callback/UUID) before the first start. Taken into account once, when the provider is created. Generate it with uuidgen. | `random UUID` | no (yes with bundled Pocket ID) | `0b8e6c1e-5d3a-4c1f-9a77-2f6a1d4b9e10` | 0.32.0 | yes |
| `OIDC_CA_FILE` | backend | PEM file of an internal certificate authority to trust for the provider. Mount it into the backend container. | – | no | `/certs/ca.pem` | 0.32.0 | no |
| `AUTH_DOMAIN` | docker compose | Dedicated subdomain of the bundled Pocket ID. Its DNS points to the same machine. | – | bundled Pocket ID only | `auth.looty.example.org` | 0.32.0 | yes |
| `POCKET_ID_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | docker compose | Encryption key of the bundled Pocket ID. | – | bundled Pocket ID only | `openssl rand -base64 32` | 0.32.0 | yes |
| `POCKET_ID_STATIC_API_KEY` | docker compose | Admin key used once by pocket-id-init to create Looty's client. Can be removed afterwards. | – | bundled Pocket ID only | `openssl rand -hex 32` | 0.32.0 | yes |
| `LOOTY_LOCAL_ACCOUNTS` | backend | Turns on local accounts (email and password, optional two-step verification) next to or instead of OpenID Connect. Not recommended: an identity provider does it better. Off by default. Also see LOOTY_LOCAL_SIGNUP. | `false` | no | `true` | 0.45.0 | yes |
| `LOOTY_LOCAL_SIGNUP` | backend | Who can create a local account: closed (default, an administrator invites) or open (anyone with the address of the instance, then confirms their email). The first account of an empty instance becomes the administrator with the code printed in the backend logs. | `closed` | no | `open` | 0.45.0 | yes |

## Security and network

| Variable | Service | Role | Default | Required | Example | Since | Compose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LOOTY_SECRET_KEY` | backend | Key that encrypts stored secrets (CalDAV passwords, AI keys, Jupyter tokens). Keep it with your backups: without it those secrets are lost. | `generated in uploads/.secret.key` | recommended | `openssl rand -base64 32` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `LOOTY_DEV_LOGIN` | backend | Development only: lets anyone sign in as any user by email. NEVER enable it on a real instance. | `false` | no | `false` | 0.1.0 | no |
| `CALDAV_ALLOW_PRIVATE` | backend | Allow external CalDAV servers on a private network or over http (for example an internal Nextcloud). | `false` | no | `true` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `JUPYTER_ALLOW_PRIVATE` | backend | Allow project Jupyter servers on a private network or over http. | `false` | no | `true` | 0.29.0 | yes |
| `AI_ALLOW_PRIVATE` | backend | Allow AI providers on a private network or over http (for example Ollama on the same machine). Also allowed when CALDAV_ALLOW_PRIVATE is true. | `false` | no | `true` | 0.34.1 | no |
| `PUSH_ALLOW_PRIVATE` | backend | Tests only: accept a local push service (http, private network). | `false` | no | `false` | 0.1.0 | no |
| `LOOTY_METRICS_TOKEN` | backend | Turns on the Prometheus endpoint /metrics (also /api/metrics), read with the header Authorization: Bearer <token>. At least 16 characters; without it the endpoint does not exist. | – | no | `a-long-random-secret` | 0.43.0 | no |
| `WEBHOOKS_ALLOW_PRIVATE` | backend | Lets workspace webhooks call private network addresses (localhost, 10.x, 192.168.x…) and plain http, for example an n8n on the same network. By default webhooks only reach public https addresses. | `false` | no | `true` | 0.44.0 | no |

## Email

| Variable | Service | Role | Default | Required | Example | Since | Compose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SMTP_HOST` | backend | Outgoing mail server. Fallback: email is better configured in Administration > Email. With SMTP_HOST and SMTP_FROM unset, email is off. | – | no | `smtp.example.org` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `SMTP_FROM` | backend | Sender address. | – | with SMTP_HOST | `looty@example.org` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `SMTP_FROM_NAME` | backend | Sender name. | `Looty` | no | `Looty` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `SMTP_PORT` | backend | Mail server port. | `587 (starttls), 465 (tls), 25 (none)` | no | `587` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `SMTP_SECURITY` | backend | Connection security: starttls, tls or none. | `starttls` | no | `tls` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `SMTP_USERNAME` | backend | Mail server user. | – | no | `looty` | 0.1.0 | yes |
| `SMTP_PASSWORD` | backend | Mail server password. | – | no | – | 0.1.0 | yes |

## Integrations and features

| Variable | Service | Role | Default | Required | Example | Since | Compose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CALENDAR_DEFAULT_TZ` | backend | Default time zone of calendars, statistics and backups (IANA name). | `UTC` | no | `Europe/Paris` | 0.1.0 | no |
| `MOODLE_POLL_SECONDS` | backend | Delay between two Moodle refreshes for notifications (minimum 10). | `300` | no | `600` | 0.8.0 | no |
| `MOODLE_CACHE_MB` | backend | Total size of the Moodle offline cache per instance, in MB. | `500` | no | `500` | 0.22.2 | no |
| `MOODLE_CACHE_FILE_MB` | backend | Largest Moodle file kept in the offline cache, in MB. | `25` | no | `25` | 0.22.2 | no |
| `SITES_BASE_URL` | backend | Address used to serve project web sites, if different from BASE_URL. | `BASE_URL` | no | `https://sites.looty.example.org` | 0.10.0 | no |
| `SITES_SANDBOX` | backend | Serve project web sites in a sandbox. Set false to turn the sandbox off. | `true` | no | `false` | 0.10.0 | no |
| `LATEX_BIN_DIR` | backend | Folder of the LaTeX compiler, when it is not in PATH. | `PATH` | no | `/usr/local/texlive/bin` | 0.10.0 | no |
| `BACKUP_DIR` | backend | Folder of the backups made from Administration. | `backups` | no | `/app/backups` | 0.7.0 | no |

## Public demo

| Variable | Service | Role | Default | Required | Example | Since | Compose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LOOTY_DEMO` | backend | Public demo mode: replaces sign-in with « Enter the demo » and a throwaway copy per visitor. Never on a real instance; use docker-compose.demo.yml. | `false` | no | `false` | 0.30.0 | yes |
| `LOOTY_DEMO_MAX_COPIES` | backend | Demo: simultaneous copies. | `30` | no | `30` | 0.30.0 | yes |
| `LOOTY_DEMO_COPIES_PER_IP_HOUR` | backend | Demo: copies per address and per hour (the reverse proxy must send X-Forwarded-For). | `5` | no | `5` | 0.30.0 | yes |
| `LOOTY_DEMO_MAX_FILE_MB` | backend | Demo: size of one upload, in MB. | `2` | no | `2` | 0.30.0 | yes |
| `LOOTY_DEMO_MAX_COPY_MB` | backend | Demo: total size per copy, in MB. | `20` | no | `20` | 0.30.0 | yes |
| `LOOTY_DEMO_RESET_HOUR` | backend | Demo: hour (0 to 23, in CALENDAR_DEFAULT_TZ, UTC otherwise) of the nightly full reset, which deletes every copy even if it is not expired. Any other value, such as off, turns it off. | `3` | no | `3` | 0.50.0 | yes |

## Advanced

| Variable | Service | Role | Default | Required | Example | Since | Compose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | backend, collaboration | Port the service listens on. Docker images already set it. | `8080 (backend), 8082 (collaboration)` | no | `8080` | 0.1.0 | no |
| `LOOTY_UPDATE_CHECK` | backend | Lets the instance status page ask GitHub (at most every 6 hours) whether a newer web version exists. Off by default: the server makes no outgoing call for it. | `false` | no | `true` | 0.43.0 | no |
| `LOOTY_STUN_URLS` | backend | STUN servers (comma-separated) that browsers use to find a direct path for voice calls. Only the IP addresses of the participants are shown to the STUN server, never audio. Use your own server to avoid the public one. | `stun:stun.l.google.com:19302` | no | `stun:stun.example.org:3478` | 0.54.0 | no |
| `LOOTY_CALL_MAX_PARTICIPANTS` | backend, collaboration | Initial maximum of people in one voice call (2 to 12), used until the administrator sets a number in Administration > Instance > Calls. Calls are peer-to-peer: each person sends audio to every other one, so large calls use more bandwidth on the participants' side. | `6` | no | `4` | 0.54.0 | no |
| `LOOTY_TURN_URLS` | backend | TURN relay addresses (comma-separated, turn: or turns:) offered to browsers for voice calls behind restrictive firewalls. Needs LOOTY_TURN_SECRET. Set automatically by the installer with --turn. | – | no | `turn:looty.example.org:3478?transport=udp,turn:looty.example.org:3478?transport=tcp` | 0.54.0 | no |
| `LOOTY_TURN_SECRET` | backend | Secret shared with coturn (`static-auth-secret`, `use-auth-secret`). Looty uses it to give each signed-in person a temporary TURN login (valid LOOTY_TURN_TTL seconds); the secret itself never reaches browsers. | – | no | `(random, 32+ characters)` | 0.54.0 | no |
| `LOOTY_TURN_TTL` | backend | Validity of the temporary TURN logins, in seconds (300 to 604800). A call longer than this loses the relay (direct connections are not affected). | `86400` | no | `3600` | 0.54.0 | no |
| `TURN_SECRET` | docker compose | Shared secret of the optional coturn service (written by the installer with --turn). Passed to the backend as LOOTY_TURN_SECRET. | – | no | – | 0.54.0 | no |
| `TURN_EXTERNAL_IP` | docker compose | Public IP of the server when it sits behind NAT (cloud instances): coturn announces it as the relay address. | – | no | `203.0.113.10` | 0.54.0 | no |
| `TURN_MIN_PORT` | docker compose | First UDP port of the relay range of coturn. Keep the range small (about 20 ports per simultaneous relayed participant) and open it on the firewall. | `49160` | no | `49160` | 0.54.0 | no |
| `TURN_MAX_PORT` | docker compose | Last UDP port of the relay range of coturn. | `49200` | no | `49200` | 0.54.0 | no |
| `ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS` | backend | Days between a deletion request and the actual deletion of an account (1 to 90). Until then the person can cancel. | `14` | no | `30` | 0.43.0 | no |
| `LOOTY_SITE_URL` | backend | Address of the site the apps ask for updates (/api/releases), instead of the official one. | `address in releases.json` | no | `https://looty.example.org` | 0.16.7 | no |
| `BACKEND_URL` | web interface, collaboration | Internal address of the backend, for the web interface and the collaboration service. The compose files set it. | `http://backend:8080` | no | `http://backend:8080` | 0.1.0 | no |
| `COLLAB_URL` | web interface | Internal address of the collaboration service, for the web interface (/collab). | `http://collaboration:8082` | no | `http://collaboration:8082` | 0.1.0 | no |
